::: {.notes}
Each bullet on the left and its tile on the right share the same
`data-fragment-index`, so they appear together in a single click —
without the explicit index, reveal.js's default .incremental behavior
would only step through the left column and show every tile on slide
entry.

Tiles are positioned freely (a collage, not a stacked list): each
`.use-area-tile` div's `top/left/width/height` are percentages of the
`.use-area-collage` box, following the same pattern as the `.frame-overlay`
circles/boxes on the "Anatomy at a Glance" slide below. Drag them around
by editing those four numbers — they don't need to line up in a grid,
and can overlap if you want a true collage look.

Keep `top + height <= 100` and `left + width <= 100` for every tile.
This isn't enforced anywhere and the collage box clips (`.use-area-tile`
has `overflow: hidden` set on itself, but the collage box itself doesn't
clip its children — a tile that runs past 100% just extends past the
bottom/right edge of the collage and, since the collage now correctly
fills all the way to the slide's own edge — see the sizing rule in
styles/custom.scss — that means past the edge of the *slide*, silently
under the footer with no visual clipping to warn you. Two tiles
("Provide Service" at top:80/height:30, "Harvest Energy" at
top:67/height:50) shipped over 100% and only became visibly obvious
once an unrelated flex-sizing bug that had been artificially shrinking
the collage got fixed — check the arithmetic by hand when adding or
resizing a tile, don't just eyeball one window size.

To swap in a real photo for one of the placeholder tiles:

1. Replace the `::: {.use-area-placeholder} ... :::` div with
   `![](media/your-image.png)`, keeping it inside the same
   `.use-area-tile` div (the caption span stays as a sibling below it).
2. Resize/reposition the tile on the board via that tile's own
   `top/left/width/height` in its `style` attribute.
3. To reposition or zoom the photo *within* its tile (crop into part of
   a wide shot, recenter a subject) without changing the tile's
   footprint, set `--img-scale`, `--img-shift-x`, and/or `--img-shift-y`
   on the image itself — see the "Move things or people" tile for a
   worked example (scaled up 1.4x and shifted up-left to frame the
   aircraft fuselage rather than the handler).

Each tile with a real photo also carries a `.use-area-info` div (see the
"Move things or people" and "Harvest Energy" tiles): a full-tile overlay
that's invisible until you hover (or Tab-focus, for keyboard users) the
tile, then fades in over the photo showing a short description and a
"Source ↗" link back to where the image came from. To fill one in,
replace its placeholder description text and swap the `TODO-add-source-url`
href for the real source page. When adding a tooltip to a newly-swapped
photo, copy the same `.use-area-info` block in as a sibling after the
image/caption.
:::

## UAV Market 2026

![](media/drone-market-environment-map-2026.png)

::: {.footer}
Alt+click the map to zoom in (Option+click on Mac, Ctrl+click on Linux)
:::

::: {.notes}
Source PDF (`media/drone-market-environment-map-2026.pdf`) is a single dense
infographic page, so an `<img>` tag can't display it directly — browsers
don't rasterize PDFs through `<img>`. Regenerate the PNG in two steps if the
source PDF changes:

  pdftoppm -png -r 150 drone-market-environment-map-2026.pdf \
    drone-market-environment-map-2026 -singlefile

  uv run python -c "
  from PIL import Image
  im = Image.open('drone-market-environment-map-2026.png').convert('RGB')
  im.convert('P', palette=Image.ADAPTIVE, colors=256).save(
      'drone-market-environment-map-2026.png', optimize=True)
  "

150dpi on the ~32x20in page gives a 4843x2953 PNG, big enough to stay crisp
when zoomed. The 256-color quantize step matters here: this project sets
`embed-resources: true`, so every render (including `quarto preview`'s
live-reload re-render on every save) base64-inlines the full PNG into the
HTML. At the raw 150dpi export (~5.9MB, mostly anti-aliasing noise on a
flat logo-grid infographic — no photos/gradients to lose) that inflates to
a ~7.9MB inline blob and was heavy enough to make `quarto preview`'s reload
flaky (page not opening into the deck correctly), while a plain static
`python -m http.server` of the already-finished render loaded it fine.
Quantizing to a 256-color palette (still visually identical for this
image — verified by diffing crops) cuts it to ~1.7MB with no visible loss.
If a future replacement image is more photographic and quantizing would
show, drop the `colors=256` step and re-check whether preview is still
usable — worst case, look at scoping `embed-resources` out of preview-time
config rather than shipping a multi-MB inline image.

The image is left as the slide's sole top-level element (no wrapping div,
no on-slide caption) so Quarto's `auto-stretch` revealjs option (on by
default project-wide, see `_quarto.yml`) can size it via reveal.js's
`r-stretch` class — this measures slide layout in reveal's own
pre-transform coordinate space, so it fills the available height correctly
at any window size. A `max-height: Xvh` CSS rule (tried first, reverted)
does NOT work for this: reveal.js scales the whole 1050x700 slide via a
CSS transform to fit the viewport, but `vh` resolves against the *real*
browser viewport rather than that transformed coordinate space — so on a
large/fullscreen window the image comes out oversized in slide-space and
overflow pushes any other on-slide content out past the visible, clipped
slide edge (only came back into view once the window was shrunk enough to
drop the scale factor below 1).

The "Alt+click to zoom" hint is a per-slide `.footer` override (see the
`footer` key in `document-reveal-content.yml`) rather than an ordinary
on-slide paragraph, for two reasons: a plain paragraph would break the
"sole top-level element" condition `auto-stretch` needs above, and
`.footer` is rendered by Quarto's support.js as `position: fixed` on
`.reveal` itself (see `plugins/support/footer.css`) — i.e. positioned
against the real viewport like reveal's other UI chrome (controls,
progress bar), not against the scaled slide box, so it can't be pushed
off-slide the way the vh-sized image was.

The hint text itself: reveal.js's Zoom plugin's default modifier key is
Alt on Mac/Windows and Ctrl on Linux (`zoom.js`, `/Linux/.test(navigator.
platform) ? "ctrl" : "alt"`) — don't tell people to just "Ctrl+click" as a
platform-agnostic instruction, since on Mac that's not the zoom modifier
and instead triggers the browser's native right-click-style context menu
("Save Image As…") on an image, which is what was happening before.

This slide intentionally skips the `.frame-wrap`/`.frame-overlay` callout
pattern used elsewhere on this page (see "Anatomy at a Glance" below) —
that pattern is for pointing fixed annotations at a few features of a
photo, not for making a dense map broadly legible.
:::
